title.narrative: Provision of Life-Saving Cash, Shelter and Non-Food Items Assistance to Flood-Affected Households in Aweil East, Nasir, Mayendit, Rubkona and Fangak, South Sudan

description.narrative: As the lead agency for Shelter and Non-Food Item (S-NFI) Pipeline management, and with a wide operational frontline presence, IOM will provide life-saving assistance within the immediate flood response. This will include replenishing, transporting and distributing S-NFI in-kind supplies and providing cash assistance to the most vulnerable flood-affected populations. The project is in line with the CERF and S-NFI Cluster sector specific objectives, prioritizing the most urgent and life-saving S-NFI static and mobile responses, S-NFI supplies for newly displaced or vulnerable populations, as well as host communities who are unable to meet their basic emergency S-NFI needs as a result of the floods. Through in-kind S-NFI support and cash assistance, IOM aims to meet the emergency S-NFI needs of 186,546 flood-affected individuals, including women, child-headed households and persons with disabilities, in Unity, Upper Nile, Northern Bahr El Ghazal and Jonglei States. This intervention will contribute to improve their living conditions while ensuring safety and dignity. In particular, IOM will distribute S-NFI kits to 171,000 individuals (28,500 households) in the prioritized counties of Aweil East (10,490 households), Rubkona (10,442 households), Fangak (3,778households), Mayendit (2,034 households) and Nasir (1,756 households). Due to availability of functional markets in Aweil East and Rubkona, IOM will provide unconditional cash assistance to 15,546 individuals (2,591 households) meeting the immediate life-saving needs of those affected by floods. In heavily flooded areas such as Fangak, Nasir, and Mayendit, where logistical challenges may hinder in-kind assistance, IOM will prioritize cash-based responses. This will be done by reallocating last-mile transportation costs, budgeted under the CERF Rapid Response Allocation, to expand the cash response, provided essential shelter materials (e.g., local poles, grass, bamboo) are available from host communities or nearby towns.In addition, under this CERF allocation, IOM will support the S-NFI Core pipeline by replenishing 28,500 emergency S-NFI kits to meet the urgent shelter and NFI needs of 171,000 individuals in targeted locations. The Core Pipeline serves as a central repository of emergency shelter and NFI humanitarian supplies in South Sudan which facilitates coordinated bulk procurement, warehousing and storage of emergency preparedness supplies at logistic warehouse hubs in Juba, Bor, Bentiu, Malakal and Wau. From these hubs, S-NFI Cluster partner organizations can access the emergency S-NFI supplies to timely respond to emergencies across the country. Through this CERF Rapid Response Allocation, the Core Pipeline will support South Sudan’s emergency preparedness and response in prioritized counties through the provision of in-kind assistance, including plastic sheets, rubber rope, mosquito nets and blankets, to the most vulnerable households in Aweil East, Rubkona, Fangak, Nasir and Mayendit counties.
